summary: The case involved a dispute over entitlement of Nursing Assistants in the Border Security Force to receive Nursing Allowance at par with Staff Nurses. The High Court had upheld their claim, emphasizing similar duties and holding educational qualifications cannot be a ground for denial. The Supreme Court reversed this, relying on precedents affirming that pay structures and allowances may lawfully vary based on educational qualifications and experience. It held that Nursing Assistants, lacking the requisite qualifications and registration for the post of Staff Nurse, are not entitled to equal nursing allowance, and that the Executive has discretion in determining pay scales. The impugned judgment was set aside.
legal_provisions_cited: Punjab State Cooperative Milk Producers Federation Limited v. Balbir Kumar Walia, (2021) 8 SCC 784
Director of Elementary Education, Odisha v. Pramod Kumar Sahoo, (2019) 10 SCC 674
Secretary, Department of Personnel v. T.V.L.N. Mallikarjuna Rao, (2015) 3 SCC 653
final_judgment: The appeal is allowed. The impugned judgment of the Gauhati High Court is quashed and set aside. The original writ petition is dismissed.
